articles.headline: What grade did PFF give Spencer Fano in Week 8 against the Steelers?

body: The NFL season will sometimes show us what we want to see from players; other times, we may see something bad when it isn't there. For fans and media, it's essential to have a way to verify and balance information to prevent favoritism or bias from being portrayed in a negative light.

He wrote of his performance, saying, "Fano struggled mightily against Pittsburgh’s vaunted defensive line in Week 8. He allowed a season-high eight pressures, which is more than he had given up in the previous four games combined. Those efforts led to him recording a subpar 43.1 PFF pass-blocking grade. Fano also committed three penalties on the day. His work in the ground game against Pittsburgh was a tad better, but Week 8 was mostly one to forget for Fano."

articles.headline: Xavier Becerra snaps at reporters for asking about his plans for office in first press conference: ‘Don’t play this game!’
keyFacts: California Governor-elect Xavier Becerra emphasized affordability in his first post-election press conference while declining to make specific commitments before taking office.
Becerra stated that all options regarding tax policy, healthcare, and energy are on the table to reduce the state's cost of living.
Becerra promised a close partnership with legislative leaders and stated that announcements regarding his transition team would come soon.
body: California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra said “everything should be on the table” to make the state more affordable in his first public statement since election night — before bristling over questions about what he’ll actually do.
“I’m no longer a candidate; I’m now the governor-elect. So I will take this very seriously,” Becerra said.
“But, guys, don’t play this game about asking me to commit, because I didn’t get elected doing that.”

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Becerra, who appeared alongside Assembly Speaker Robert Rivas and Senate President Pro Tem Monique Limón, promised a close partnership with legislative leaders and said announcements about his transition team would come soon.
The three Democrats presented a united front on affordability, though Becerra offered few specifics about how he would deliver relief on housing, health care and energy.
“The public made it very clear we should be focused on job one, two, and three, and that is cost of living, cost of living, cost of living,” he said.
Asked whether that could include cutting taxes, Becerra left the door open — but he also suggested that wealthy residents should pay a higher tax rate than they do currently.

“I think everything should be on the table,” Becerra said. “By the way, you’re probably going to be hearing me say that a lot, whether it’s on energy, whether it’s on revenue and tax policy, whether it’s on healthcare, why should we take anything off the table?”
That openness gave way to a defensive posture when questioned about his commitments to making health coverage more affordable.
“You want me to make a commitment to families without knowing what the budget will be, without knowing where the votes are, and that’s just playing politics the wrong way,” Becerra said.
He pointed to his record of expanding access and lowering health care costs, saying he intended to continue that work as governor.
“A lot of other folks make these wild promises, and they’re not the governor-elect,” Becerra said.
On taxes, Becerra said he wanted to determine who was paying their “fair share,” pointing to the state Department of Finance and Legislative Analyst’s Office as sources of expertise.
He said Proposition 40 — the billionaire tax measure he and Newsom both opposed — had sent a signal about concerns over unequal taxation.

“If you’re paying at a tax rate in California that’s lower than the tax rate of a teacher, a firefighter, a nurse, a police officer, and you’re making way more money than they are, in my book, you’re not paying your fair share,” Becerra said.
Rivas cautioned that Tuesday’s results should not be mistaken for a blanket endorsement of Democratic leadership.
“Our mandate is to do things differently,” Rivas said. “People want change.”

Becerra, who congratulated Nithya Raman on her win in the Los Angeles mayor’s race, also answered multiple questions in Spanish, discussing affordability and protections for immigrants while acknowledging California cannot override federal law.
Asked about choosing a finance director, he made an awkward attempt at humor, saying he would like “someone [who] can pull money off of trees.”

“Since I suspect that’ll be tough to find, we will look for someone who knows their numbers, who can do this well, has experience in balancing a budget as large as the budget of the state of California.”
Becerra ended by suggesting he will not be doing grandstanding in that process.
“I ran on my record of what I’ve done, and I have expanded access to healthcare. I have lowered healthcare costs, and that’s what I intend to do again,” Becerra said.
“But I can’t make a commitment without knowing what exactly I face, because I don’t think any voter, any taxpayer, any Californian wants to have a governor who’s still acting like a politician.”

articles.headline: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
keyFacts: OpenAI announced new commitments for data center projects, including a decision to stop using non-disclosure agreements with public officials.
OpenAI stated the policy shift follows recent midterms where voters opposed data center expansion, and aims to address scrutiny over hidden discussions.
OpenAI also committed to paying the full cost of its electricity and required infrastructure while publishing expected job creation numbers.
body: Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.
OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments.

Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects.

OpenAI’s additional commitments include paying “the full cost” of electricity it uses and the “infrastructure needed to serve us.” It will make opportunities for local communities by publishing the jobs it expects to create and by reporting on hiring. And every future “compute campus” (its rebranding phrase for data centers) the company owns and operates will have a “local compact” that includes the commitments and will reflect “local priorities,” OpenAI says.

articles.headline: Mom of slain cop breaks down over Gavin Newsom’s mass communtation of death row killers
keyFacts: California Governor Gavin Newsom commuted the death sentences of all 548 condemned inmates in the state.
Phyllis Loya, whose police officer son Larry Lasater was killed in 2005, expressed immense anger and emotional pain over the decision.
Loya accused Newsom of political motivation and claimed the governor ignored the will of California voters.
body: The reverberations from California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s decision to commute the death sentences of all 548 condemned inmates in California has left surviving loved ones reeling, including one 78-year-old mother who broke down in tears in an interview with The California Post.
Phyllis Loya is the mother of Larry Lasater. He was shot and killed on April 23, 2005, while working as a police officer in Pittsburg, California.

Lasater was attempting to arrest two robbery suspects that had targeted a supermarket and bank, according to local police. Alexander Rashad Hamilton, hiding in a bush, shot and killed Lasater and was later sentenced to death — until Newsom decided to spare his life Thursday.

Loya said her first reaction when she heard about Newsom’s act was “immense anger.” She said she found out while leaving the gym with friends, proclaiming, “This is the worst day of my life.”
“It’s been very tough. It’s very emotional,” the mother said.
Loya pinned the pain she was feeling on the governor. She told The Post she didn’t believe in Newsom’s stated reason of abiding by his morals in commuting the sentences.
She instead accused the governor of being a “political animal” for dropping news of his decision right after the midterms, which showed a Democratic trouncing of Republicans.
“He wants to be president. So I was thinking he was testing the water, and the election made him go for it today. That was the only thing that held off his decision,” Loya said.
“Does Gavin Newsom ever talk about the victims? No, he doesn’t,” she added.
She noted that Newsom, when he first ran for governor, told editorial boards at the time that he would “follow the will of the people” when asked on the death penalty.
He never did, Loya said, pointing to Newsom’s 2019 moratorium on executions and the fact California voters have voted to keep the death penalty on the books.

“He doesn’t care about the will of the people. He cares about what’s going to be good for Gavin Newsom. And if I sound bitter, I am bitter,” she said.

For many years, Loya said she’s already been struggling with going to court dates for the case of the other robbery suspect in her son’s death, who was sentenced to life. Newsom’s mass commutation is a double blow for her, she said.

“To get retraumatized, except see, this time, it’s not the killer retraumatizing us. I’m being retraumatized by laws passed by the legislatures or by the governor. That’s retraumatizing,” she said. “That’s who’s retraumatizing me, not the killer. The putting the knife in and twisting it, that’s the Legislature and the governor.”
For the now spared killer who has a life sentence without the possibility of parole, Loya said she had no confidence in the justice system to maintain that punishment.
Many victim advocates have been protesting the state’s parole board and lawmakers for supposedly loosening parole terms or granting more accessways to parole.
Loya said she wanted the public to know how good of a person his son was. Lasater was a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and had served with the Pittsburg Police Department for five years.
The killing of Lasater not only deprived a life but also took away a father. His son was born two-and-a-half months after his death.
“The closest my son ever came to holding his son was a sonogram that was buried with him in his lifeless hands,” Loya said while crying.
“Those bullets that killed my son killed a part of me and a part of everybody that loved him.”

articles.headline: Hegseth not being considered for Blackburn’s Tennessee Senate seat: Report
keyFacts: Sen. Marsha Blackburn won Tennessee's gubernatorial election and will appoint her Senate successor when sworn in as governor in January.
Multiple reports state Blackburn is not considering War Secretary Pete Hegseth for the vacant Senate seat.
A source close to Blackburn called Hegseth's consideration Washington spin, while other Tennessee politicians have expressed interest.
body: Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) is reportedly not considering War Secretary Pete Hegseth as her replacement in the upper chamber once she is sworn in as Tennessee’s governor.

Blackburn defeated Democrat Jerri Green in Tennessee’s gubernatorial election on Tuesday, holding 45.49% of the vote compared to Green’s 42.98%, with 98.9% of the vote counted, according to the Associated Press . Blackburn announced that she would hold off on retiring from the Senate until she is sworn in to her gubernatorial seat in January, meaning she will be in charge of appointing her successor for the remainder of her unexpired term.

Several candidates have already reportedly thrown their hat in the ring for consideration, including Hegseth, who moved to Sumner County, Tennessee, with his family in 2022 ahead of his relocation to Washington, D.C., for his job leading the Pentagon. As murmurs swirl of Democrats considering a possible impeachment of Hegseth as they retake the majority in the House in 2027, Hegseth could avoid the articles if Blackburn appoints him to the upper chamber.
But according to multiple reports, including the Associated Press , Blackburn is not considering tapping Hegseth.
A source close to Blackburn told Punchbowl News that Hegseth is “not being considered.”

“This is nothing more than Washington, D.C., spin from a bunch of consultants with nothing better to do. The Blackburn team is focused on the transition, not entertaining baseless speculation. Dc won’t pick the next senator,” the source said .
The Washington Examiner has reached out to Blackburn’s office and campaign for comment.

Hegseth, who recently attended a University of Tennessee home football game against the University of Alabama, is not the only Tennessean considering a run. Reps. Tim Burchett (R-TN) and Chuck Fleischmann (R-TN), former Knox County Mayor Glenn Jacobs, and former private prison CEO Damon Hininger have each expressed interest.
Burchett said in a statement to the Washington Examiner that he has “made no bones about the fact that I would be honored to represent Tennessee in the United States Senate.”

articles.headline: Trump signs proclamation to try to prevent changes to gold-covered Oval Office
keyFacts: Donald Trump signed a proclamation declaring the Oval Office and Cabinet Room national monuments to prevent future administrations from altering his designs.
The announcement follows midterm election defeats for Trump's party, which resulted in Democrats securing control of Congress.
Trump said the proclamation ensures the White House West Wing rooms will not be touched or destroyed by anyone.
body: Donald Trump signed a proclamation on Thursday that he says will prevent future administrations from changing his design of the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, spaces which he declared as national monuments that should be preserved.

In the days since his party suffered historic defeats in the midterm elections, the president has seemingly turned his attention to the many renovation projects he has begun across the nation’s capital. Sitting behind the Resolute Desk on Thursday, Trump declared the Oval Office a “national monument”.
“I’m going to be signing a document which will make them into a landmark for the ages,” he told reporters in the gold-covered Oval Office.

According to the president, the proclamation would ensure the West Wing rooms would not be “touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape”.
“I just thought it was very important that nobody be allowed to come and take it down and try and do something with it,” he said.

“Every once in a while they’ll look and they’ll say, oh, maybe what we’ll do is we’ll put some glass up that’s a little bit better or something, and I say no, you’re not going to do anything. We’re going to leave this as it is,” he continued.
“If anyone ever decides to come and start knocking down walls, you’ll call me wherever I may be, and I will come back here and I will make sure it never happens.”

Since returning to office, Trump has embarked on a series of White House “beautification” projects, most notably the demolition of the East Wing to make way for a $600m ballroom, as well the building of a permanent granite helipad on the South Lawn.

Speaking to reporters from the Oval Office, the president defended his wider renovation work at the White House, saying the building’s exterior had suffered from years of deterioration. He pointed to cracked windows, damaged stonework and broken decorative features, saying he had paid for repairs and hired skilled workers to restore them.
“When you looked at that wall one year ago, it was badly damaged from years of service,” he said, adding that exterior columns had also been in “horrible shape”.

On the desk next to where he signed the proclamation was a red baseball cap emblazoned with the word “Veto” – an explicit reminder of his threat to block the legislative priorities and bills passed by the new Democratic-controlled Congress next year.

Democrats made significant gains in several traditionally Republican states where Trump had previously won, including Texas, Kansas, South Carolina and Iowa, by campaigning on issues including affordability and tackling corruption, while also securing control of Congress.

Trump’s opulent redesign of the Oval Office has drawn criticism, including from former president Barack Obama, who recently joked that “he’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere.”
Obama’s remark prompted a coordinated response from the White House, with treasury secretary Scott Bessent appearing to hit back by dining at a Cheesecake Factory.

In a final appeal ahead of the midterm elections, Trump held a press conference highlighting the delayed results of his $14m renovation of the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool, while blaming Joe Biden for the algae that had accumulated in its waters.
“This was in the Biden era … Look, it’s not an easy thing. The algae is brutal. It forms easily. All you saw was dirt and filth and paper and everything else for years,” Trump said on Monday.
Two days later, as the scale of his party’s staggering losses came into focus, Trump led a media tour of the White House Ballroom construction site, where he marveled at the renovations to come.
“The whole thing is a miracle,” he said.

articles.headline: 'Families need reliable electricity': OpenAI pledges to try and provide 'a national effort to support affordable, reliable electricity for families and businesses' living near its data centers
keyFacts: OpenAI launched the Grid Protectors Program to protect residents and businesses near its data centers from potential power outages.
The program is launching at a planned data center campus in Effingham County, Georgia, through an agreement with Georgia Power.
OpenAI stated that the project will provide flexible power demand to support local households during extreme weather conditions.
body: - OpenAI launches new program to protect residents and businesses near its data centers from power outages
- The Grid Protectors Program is designed to prevent OpenAI campuses from “hogging” all the power
- A new development in Effingham County, Georgia, will pioneer the program

OpenAI wants to protect local communities situated around its data centers from power outages, and has launched a new program intended to deliver both reliability and affordability to nearby residents and businesses.

The Grid Protectors Program is launching with the planned Effingham County, Georgia data center campus, which features an agreement with Georgia Power to make power available in a flexible demand scenario, which should cover demand for around 700,000 households.

OpenAI’s future facilities are designed to be more flexible in how they demand power from the grid, and the Grid Protectors Program viewed as a “starting point” for improved reliability for homes, businesses, and of course data campuses.
Grid Protectors pilot

The Grid Protector Program certainly seems a step in the right direction from OpenAI. It comes against a backdrop of growing concerns over the power requirements of AI data centers and protests over their approval, invariably in locations where residents are resistant.
OpenAI says the pilot site at Effingham County incorporates its agreement with Georgia Power to accommodate “up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response.”

This is intended to ensure local residential and business properties have the power available “to help keep air conditioning running in hundreds of thousands of homes during extreme heat. For scale, that is equivalent to the average electricity demand of roughly 700,000 households.”
OpenAI says this is more than enough to cover the combined households of Washington, D.C., and Boston.

Financial assurances

By working to offer communities assurances of flexible energy at its new site, OpenAI clearly hopes that its upcoming data centers are recognized as more suited to locations that have recently come under fire.

Perhaps they want to be a part of those communities? The launch announcement adds that its new compute facilities are more flexible than older facilities, and OpenAI is committing itself under the Grid Protectors Program to collaborate with authorities.

“We will work with utilities, regulators and policymakers to develop practical arrangements for the campuses we build in the future,” it announces, “arrangements that reflect local grid needs, help campuses support the grid when it is under pressure, and pay the costs we create. articles.headline: Bluetooth Speeds Are Set to Quadruple in 2027
keyFacts: The Bluetooth Special Interest Group unveiled Bluetooth High Data Throughput, which quadruples maximum bit rates to 7.5Mbps.
Compatible devices are expected to arrive in store shelves starting in 2027, beginning with premium wireless audio products.
The upgrade features a new physical layer that improves efficiency and helps save battery life for connected devices.
body: Wireless tech is about to get a whole lot snappier. On Thursday, the Bluetooth Special Interest Group, the trade association that oversees Bluetooth, officially unveiled Bluetooth High Data Throughput, a flagship upgrade set to arrive as part of the Bluetooth Core 7.0 standard. The revision supercharges Bluetooth Low Energy by pushing maximum bit rates to 7.5Mbps, effectively quadrupling the throughput of the existing LE 2M technology. Compatible devices are slated to hit store shelves starting in 2027.

That’s good news for phone users, tablet havers, laptop groupies, smart speaker stans and more. Bluetooth is still the most popular medium-to-short-range wireless standard for connecting devices. But this is a big rollout, and the changes will start with premium wireless, such as earbuds, with other applications following.

Those other applications could include spatial computing, exchanging AI-related info with local devices, connecting to health wearables and a host of smart home applications, like playing Spotify through an Amazon Echo Studio or dimming a smart bulb.
More from CNET

“Imagine a smartwatch that syncs hours’ worth of sensor-rich training data to your phone in seconds, smart glasses that deliver richer AI experiences by offloading data for processing, or a smart home product that completes a firmware update with virtually no user-visible downtime,” Øyvind Strøm, executive vice president of the short-range business unit at Nordic Semiconductor, said in a statement. “Bluetooth HDT paves the way for more sophisticated, data-intensive Bluetooth applications.”
A representative from the Bluetooth Special Interest Group didn’t respond to a request for comment.
What makes Bluetooth HDT so speedy?

The biggest change in this update is a new physical layer for Bluetooth. Layers are like different sections of the Bluetooth protocol, and the physical layer is the bedrock of the standard, the foundational layer involved in transmitting and receiving data signals.

Improvements in the physical layer can have very significant effects on all Bluetooth communications. In this case, new modulation schemes let the physical layer handle data more efficiently and transmit more data at once, which is why the speed increases are so significant.

These improvements also make the new standard more efficient, saving battery life in many applications. So your smart lock may last longer before you need to exchange the AA batteries, earbuds won’t need to go back in the case as fast, and so on.
Wait until next year
We know the first flagship devices are expected to appear with the technology in early 2027, but don’t have an exact date.
All we know about which specific devices will get the technology first is that it will start with wireless audio.
With protocol changes like this, it can take some time for new products to reach the market, and manufacturers may take a long time, even years, to adopt it.

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed Is Ready To Wear Ted Cruz's ‘Jihadist Leprechaun’ Insult With Pride
keyFacts: Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers by seven points in Tuesday's midterm election.
El-Sayed responded on "The View" to Islamophobic insults from Republicans, including Sen. Ted Cruz calling him a "jihadist leprechaun".
El-Sayed stated that Republicans relied on personal attacks because they lacked policy solutions for grocery costs, gas prices, and healthcare.
body: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) couldn’t help but laugh at one Republican’s ridiculous Islamophobic insult while discussing the venom that followed his campaign during a Thursday visit to “The View.”

Panelist Sunny Hostin told El-Sayed that while she knows politics aren’t pretty, she was still staggered by how “ugly” things got during his race against Republican Mike Rogers, whom El-Sayed defeated by seven points in Tuesday’s midterm election.

Hostin referenced when Vice President JD Vance said there was something “very, very evil” about El-Sayed and how Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) called the nation’s soon-to-be first Muslim senator a “jihadist leprechaun.”
“I don’t even know what that means,” Hostin said.
“I want a hat!” El-Sayed quipped.
He then argued that Republican attacks on his campaign were limited to personal smears and assaults on his faith because the GOP had nothing substantial to sell voters.

“If they had something to say about the price of gas or the price of groceries or the fact that people can’t see a doctor, they would’ve said it. But they didn’t have anything to say,” he explained, adding that he was prepared for his opponents to dangle that kind of “red meat” in front of their base.

“Here’s the problem with the red meat: It becomes an addiction,” El-Sayed went on. “Once you go there and you put that out there, then you’re forced to defend it. So what do they do? They double down. They triple down again.”

Admitting that the hate came as no surprise, El-Sayed said, “More often than not, people don’t want to actually debate the issues. Instead, they want to debase the politics, and that’s exactly what we saw.”

Panelist Joy Behar then applauded the senator-elect for handling President Donald Trump and his cronies with such poise, particularly after Trump said El-Sayed would “have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate.”
“I’ll do a metal detector all day because I have nothing to hide,” El-Sayed repeated. “But Donald, if you’re watching, a lie detector is still on the table.”

articles.headline: Duran & Osmand spark Celtic into life - but where does that leave Hogh?
keyFacts: Celtic substitutes Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran scored three goals to secure a 3-2 comeback victory against Besiktas in the Europa League.
Manager Martin O'Neill stated that the substitutions were part of a planned rotation strategy to re-energize the team during a busy schedule.
Club record signing Kasper Hogh struggled during the match, raising questions about whether Duran will replace him as the starting central striker.
body: - Published
With an hour gone at Parkhead on Thursday, hope in the stands was in short supply.
Celtic were 1-0 down against Besiktas and heading towards a fourth straight defeat in this season's Europa League.
Manager Martin O'Neill turned to his bench for a spark, bringing on Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran to replace Sebastian Tounekti and James Forrest out wide.
The impact was almost instantaneous.
Osmand's first touch nestled in the bottom corner of Alexander Nubel's goal, just 43 seconds after the 20-year-old attacker came on.
All of a sudden, Celtic had a threat in behind and Besiktas looked rattled.
Then, on 77 minutes, O'Neill withdrew Kasper Hogh after another underwhelming display from the club record signing and moved Duran through the middle.
Again it had the desired effect.
Osmand played Duran through with a delightful pass and the Colombian rounded Nubel before slotting Celtic into the lead.

Orkun Kokcu levelled for Besiktas with a fine strike, but Duran had the final say two minutes later, controlling Kieran Tierney's scuffed shot and beating Nubel from close range to send the home support into ecstasy.

"Everything changed with the subs; Osmand coming on and Duran going through the middle," former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov said on TNT Sports. "They freed up space for Nygren and Baur. It was a really positive 30 minutes."
Not since Johannes Edvaldsson against Jeunesse d'Esch in the European Cup in September 1977 had a Celtic substitute scored twice in Europe (excluding qualifiers).

"Osmand came on, first touch put the ball in the net and that's really difficult, he can definitely score a goal. Duran has been fabulous for us all season no matter where he plays," O'Neill said of his goalscorers.
The Northern Irishman was asked whether it was a case of inspired substitutions or rather evidence that he should have started his best players.
"I'm not standing up for myself, not at all," he said.
"It was in design to do exactly what it did. We've played nine games in 25 days, some players needed a breather and you can get re-energised from coming on the field.
"I'm going to say that that was our plan and those players were going to come on the pitch at some point in the game."
Numbers point to Duran as solution
The contrast between Celtic's attacking play with Hogh leading the line and with Duran through the middle was stark.

The Â£11m Dane's effort cannot be questioned. He continued to battle to try to make things happen, but since arriving from Bodo/Glimt in the summer, he has now failed to score in 16 of his 17 Celtic appearances.
In 77 minutes against Besiktas, he didn't have a single shot and managed just one touch in the opposition box.
Duran, meanwhile, played just half an hour and scored two goals, had two shots, and registered four touches in the Besiktas box.
O'Neill has previously said he is unsure of his best team, but it is now obvious that Duran is Celtic's best option through the middle.
Despite Hogh's price tag, it feels inevitable he will be among the Celtic substitutes for high-stakes games.
"It'll be tough for Hogh," Hearts defender Craig Halkett said on TNT Sports. "He was the big-money singing but it's not coming off for him.
"As a player you need to keep your head down, keep working hard and hope it turns."

Osmand too appears to have pushed himself to the front of the queue to start off the left. The former Fulham man is direct and evidently has an eye for goal, with a happy knack for scoring in big games.
"This is a great team we're playing against," Osmand told TNT Sports. "Camilo [Duran] did amazing, he's such a poacher. Credit to him.
"It's a lot harder starting games. The team dug in, stayed strong and we got our rewards.
"[The goal] caught me off guard, but I'm just glad I caught it nice. I just want to come on and make something happen. So happy with tonight."

articles.headline: The New York Times reportedly in talks to buy Letterboxd for $330 million
keyFacts: The New York Times Company has entered exclusive negotiations to acquire the movie platform Letterboxd for $330 million.
Letterboxd has grown from 3 million users in 2021 to 28 million users by April.
Film studios A24 and Sony were previously interested in acquiring Letterboxd, according to the report.
body: The New York Times Company has reportedly “entered exclusive negotiations” to acquire Letterboxd for $330 million, according to a report from The New York Times itself.

Letterboxd, an online platform for movie lovers that could be compared to Goodreads for movies, has grown dramatically in recent years. Letterboxd reported 3 million users in January 2021, a figure that grew to 28 million by April of this year. More than half of its users are under 35.
Letterboxd was previously reported to be seeking a new owner. According to the Times, film studios A24 and Sony were interested in the acquisition, but A24 was priced out.

Letterboxd is free, but users can access advanced features with a paid subscription. Its projected earnings for this year are estimated at $15 million, which is only about 4.5% of what the Times is supposedly offering to buy the company for.

The New York Times Company declined to comment on the acquisition to its own paper (lol). Personally, we wouldn’t be surprised if these anonymous tips were coming from inside the house, so we’re inclined to take this report pretty seriously.

articles.headline: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
keyFacts: Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner faces pressure after a defeat by Brentford left his side 19th in the Premier League ahead of a match against Manchester City.
Leeds manager Daniel Farke admitted his side lacks the individual quality of the league's leading teams and stated their main aim is reaching 40 points.
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta insisted Martín Zubimendi remains part of his plans despite the midfielder dropping down the pecking order this season.
body: Nothing better encapsulates the dysfunction that was Everton under Farhad Moshiri than the idea that an unknown vandal with a can of spray paint could influence the club’s managerial direction. “Pereira out, Lampard in” they daubed on a wall at Goodison Park when it appeared Vítor Pereira was in line to replace Rafael Benítez in 2022. Alarmed by fan protests, the Everton board opted instead for Frank Lampard and, while his tenure ended 12 months later with the club immersed in another relegation battle, there will be appreciation for the Coventry manager when he makes a first visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday. The connection between Lampard and Evertonians was genuine and a factor in keeping the club up in 2022. Both parties will be glad to see the other emerging stronger from those troubled times. Jack Grealish, meanwhile, will again be absent for Everton after his recent disciplinary breach, although the manager, David Moyes, said: “We will be working again with Jack soon.” Andy Hunter

Back in September, when Leeds thrashed Newcastle 4-1 at Elland Road, talk of European qualification filled the West Yorkshire airwaves. Since then Daniel Farke’s side have drawn three and lost two of their ensuing Premier League games, scoring just two goals along the way. Given that their final pass has persistently let them down, optimism is turning to pessimism. Farke would call it realism. The German – who could probably do without facing Roberto De Zerbi’s improving Tottenham on Saturday – is confident his side are improving but knows they cannot expect to run before properly mastering the art of walking. “We don’t have the individual quality [of the Premier League’s leading teams],” conceded Farke on Thursday. “We have to compensate by being tactically spot on and good at winning second balls. It’s not a criticism of my players, it’s reality. The dream of Europe is allowed but we know our main aim is to reach 40 points as quickly as possible.” Louise Taylor

Martín Zubimendi has yet to start a Premier League game this season after falling down the pecking order at Arsenal and the Spain midfielder is likely to be the subject of speculation that he could seek to depart in January. The emergence of Myles Lewis-Skelly as an alternative in the No 6 position at the end of last season has had an impact on Zubimendi after he had been a regular starter for most of his debut campaign in the Premier League. The 27-year-old signed from Real Sociedad for around £55m 15 months ago and Mikel Arteta has insisted he remains an integral part of his plans. But with the Arsenal manager trying to find the right balance in his midfield after the arrival of Bruno Guimarães, Zubimendi will be hoping he gets another chance to stake his claim against Hull on Saturday after starting in the narrow win over Slavia Prague in midweek. Ed Aarons

Álvaro Arbeloa is proof that a struggling young manager working in England for the first time can bounce back after a difficult start. Arbeloa was sliding towards the sack a month ago but he has responded at Fulham, who have taken seven points from their last three games, and will hope to extend the unbeaten run when Matthias Jaissle’s inconsistent Newcastle visit Craven Cottage. It is an inviting fixture for Fulham and a big one for Newcastle, who were poor when they lost to Everton on Monday. Jaissle, hired as Eddie Howe’s replacement in the summer, is already under pressure. But the 38-year-old could take inspiration from how Arbeloa has given himself breathing space at Fulham. Jacob Steinberg

Oliver Glasner has previous. He led Wolfsburg from mid-table to the Champions League but fell out with the club hierarchy and left in 2021. Glasner next guided Eintracht Frankfurt to Europa League glory but was openly critical of the squad’s imbalance and quality in four separate outbursts and departed in 2023. His time at Crystal Palace was a great success but after accusing the Eagles’ board in January of “abandoning” his team with the sale of Marc Guéhi to Manchester City, the Austrian left this summer for Nottingham Forest, where he became the fifth head coach in less than a year. You can probably guess where this is going. After Saturday’s defeat by Brentford left Forest 19th, Glasner was typically abrasive: “If the players buy in [to my methods], I think we can have a turnaround. And if not, the sixth manager will come in.” We’ll soon find out if Glasner has won the players around with City visiting Nottingham this weekend. If Forest’s woeful form continues, Glasner may either walk or get his marching orders from trigger-happy owner Evangelos Marinakis. Michael Butler

Pierre Sage pulled no punches in his assessment of Eddie Nketiah’s career after his excellent winning goal against Fulham last week in the EFL Cup. “I think his potential is higher than his performance for the moment,” said the Crystal Palace manager. “And we have to reduce this gap – because he needs it, the team needs it.” Nketiah is now 27 and won his solitary senior cap for England in 2023 after becoming the record scorer for the under-21s while he was still at Arsenal. His chances of adding to that look unlikely these days having been relegated to third-choice striker at Selhurst Park behind Jean-Philippe Mateta and Jørgen Strand Larsen. But with Mateta suspended for three matches after Palace’s appeal over his red card against Tottenham was rejected, Sunday’s meeting with Liverpool could be another chance for Nketiah to show his ability after scoring a late winner against them in Palace’s thrilling win over Arne Slot’s side last year. EA

It has been three weeks since Brighton’s fans were savouring a famous 5-0 thrashing of arch-rivals Crystal Palace at the Amex. But the quirks of the fixture list meant that Fabian Hürzeler’s side played five successive games on the road since then, including two trips to face Manchester City. While they lost some of the momentum from the Palace victory in the defeat by Liverpool at Anfield, last week’s Premier League win over City showed they are serious contenders for the top four and perhaps even more. But Brentford’s visit to the south coast should provide a real test of those credentials as the owner, Tony Bloom, renews his rivalry with his west London counterpart Matthew Benham, who traditionally eschews his seat in the directors’ box for one in the away section. EA

Eli Junior Kroupi did not take the headlines in Bournemouth’s win over Leeds but his cheeky nutmeg and sumptuous no-look pass to set up Amine Adli for the Cherries’ second goal was a reminder of why the youngster continues to be linked with a move to Arsenal, Bayern and PSG, despite being sidelined recently. Kroupi scored 13 Premier League goals last season – only Ryan Giggs, Wayne Rooney, Michael Owen and Romelu Lukaku have reached that total as teenagers – and only Erling Haaland and Will Osula enjoyed a better goal-per-game ratio in 2025-26. Kroupi’s foot injury, sustained in pre-season, has been carefully managed but after three substitute appearances in the wins over Manchester United, Aston Villa and Leeds, will Marco Rose be tempted to start Kroupi at Ipswich? Evanilson is in red hot form as the central striker but Kroupi is just as comfortable as a No 10 and surely has to play if he is fit as Bournemouth chase a seventh consecutive win in all competitions. MB

It is not quite six months since Sunderland beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Stadium of Light and qualified for Europe for the first time in 53 years. A day when Régis Le Bris’s side eclipsed the Club World Cup holders and Enzo Le Fée upstaged Enzo Fernández concluded with Sunderland finishing seventh. During the prolonged post-match celebrations, the captain, Granit Xhaka, grabbed a microphone and declared: “This is just the beginning – we want more.” Fast forward to gloomy November and it is not quite working out like that with even the excitement of next month’s trip to Milan overshadowed by anxiety. Sunderland are bottom of the Premier League, Le Bris concedes his side are in a relegation fight and Xhaka has looked a shadow of his former self ever since Chelsea tried and failed to sign him in the summer. Is Xhaka capable of turning back time? Sunderland securing just a second league win of the season depends on it. Louise Taylor

Can Manchester United win two games of football on the bounce for the first time this season? Being able to pose this question sums up the state Michael Carrick and his side are in as they seek to build on Tuesday’s chaotic comeback victory over Roma. Aston Villa arrive five points better off than their hosts and are everything United are not: stable, upwardly mobile and boasting a manager in Unai Emery who consistently improves players and yields results. As the international break beckons after this last Premier League fixture of the weekend, will Carrick survive what could be an eighth loss in 15 matches? Possibly, if it is not another humiliation, but the truth may be that even United’s erratic executives do not currently know the answer. Jamie Jackson

articles.headline: Vance ‘privately’ blasts Netanyahu as Iran war divides Trump admin, 2028 ambitions loom
keyFacts: Reports indicated Vice President JD Vance privately accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of being wrong about the Iran war.
Vance blamed the war for Republicans losing Congress and urged President Donald Trump to pursue a negotiated settlement.
The White House is weighing whether to resume strikes against Iran, maintain pressure, or pursue a negotiated settlement.
body: Vice President JD Vance privately accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of being "wrong on everything" about the Iran war, according to reports, as disagreements over the conflict expose tensions within the Trump administration and raise questions about Vance's potential 2028 presidential ambitions.

The clash, reported by Axios Nov. 4., comes after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, with Vance publicly blaming the war for the party's defeat while urging President Donald Trump to pursue a negotiated settlement rather than renewed military strikes.
"The reason we lost is the war," Vance wrote later on Wednesday on X.
"Low-level hostility between Vance and Netanyahu is beneficial for Vance," Nathan Sachs , a senior fellow at the Middle East Institute, told Fox News Digital.

"It allows him to give some distance from the Trump administration, which has just taken a huge electoral beating, but also to position himself ... in a very different position than President Trump himself without attacking Trump."
VANCE'S SCATHING IRAN WAR POSTMORTEM PUTS POTENTIAL 2028 GOP SHOWDOWN IN FOCUS: 'EVERYONE KNOWS WHY'

Vance has also led a faction of senior administration officials urging Trump to negotiate an end to the conflict, warning that the unpopular war could cost Republicans control of Congress , according to reports.
Netanyahu, meanwhile, had urged Trump to resume strikes against Iran ahead of the midterms, but Trump held off after endorsing Netanyahu for reelection in Israel.
Sachs said Vance's main concern appeared to be the prospect of overthrowing Iran’s government after Netanyahu presented Trump with a plan for regime change .

"Many opposition leaders in Israel, nonetheless, are very skeptical of the idea that you can bring about regime change through an air campaign," Sachs said, adding that such a campaign could have the opposite effect: "you may strengthen the regime."

As previously reported by Fox News Digital, Vance had also declined to endorse Netanyahu’s reelection campaign and criticized Israeli government officials who opposed Trump's efforts to end the Iran war.

The Israeli election further complicated the relationship, Sachs said, leaving Netanyahu's political future uncertain and raising the possibility that Vance could have to work with a different Israeli leader.
NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE

"If Netanyahu is not the leader of Israel, Vance will find himself with another decision to make: does he continue with a line that is confrontational with a new Israeli leadership, or does he say, 'Well, it was all Netanyahu; now we can see a different path forward'?" Sachs said.

"Netanyahu is a very easy target here, both because there are very real differences of opinion and Netanyahu's role was important, but also because this way he can criticize the war, criticize Netanyahu, and not say any bad word about Trump."
Roughly 6 in 10 voters said U.S. military action against Iran was the wrong decision, according to the AP Voter Poll.

"I think what's remarkable here is that it's coming out now," Sachs said. "And it's part of the fact that about midnight Wednesday, the next presidential campaign in the United States began, and JD Vance is trying to position himself."
"He is breaking with the policy of President Trump, although he's doing so by criticizing Netanyahu, never Trump," the expert reiterated.
VANCE REVEALS THE TRUMP DILEMMA THAT COULD COMPLICATE HIS 2028 WHITE HOUSE AMBITIONS
Nonetheless, Vance has played a leading role in efforts to end the conflict with Iran, including direct outreach to senior Iranian officials.
Last month, he sent a letter through Qatari intermediaries to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing renewed peace negotiations.

According to Axios, the letter said any negotiations to prevent further U.S. military strikes must address Iran's nuclear program. A U.S. official said Trump backed the outreach. Rezaei later confirmed receiving the letter but said he had not responded.
"My suspicion is that J.D. Vance was operating on behalf of Trump on this," Sachs claimed.
"Trump, after the war sort of settled after the first few weeks, appointed Vice President Vance to try and negotiate the exit strategy, and Vance has been very keen on that."
Sachs also cited Vance's involvement in an earlier memorandum of understanding with Iran as further evidence of his preference for diplomacy.
"He agreed to the MOU, which has become quite notorious in the United States, giving quite a bit to the Iranians, much more than the administration is now considering reasonable."
VANCE TAKES LEAD SELLING TRUMP’S IRAN GAMBLE AS RUBIO, HEGSETH AND RATCLIFFE CEDE SPOTLIGHT ON FRAGILE DEAL
"Vance has certainly been on the side that has been trying to achieve a diplomatic breakthrough."
The White House is now weighing whether to resume major strikes against Iran, maintain economic and naval pressure or pursue a negotiated settlement.

On Thursday, Reuters reported that Tehran submitted a formal nuclear proposal to the United States through Qatari intermediaries, making further negotiations contingent on Washington addressing its seven demands.

"The real question is whether the Americans and the Iranians can approach some kind of agreement on the fundamentals, starting with freedom of navigation in the Straits of Hormuz and the cessation of hostilities," Sachs said.
For Vance, the dispute poses a political balancing act: distancing himself from a war he reportedly opposed while serving as vice president in the administration that launched it.

"He was against the war, so it would seem, but of course, he's vice president in the administration that went to war," Sachs said, describing it as a "very difficult balancing act for him electorally."

articles.headline: Hearts bruised by Thun in self-inflicted Conference League defeat
keyFacts: Hearts lost 3-1 to Thun in the UEFA Conference League after suffering a series of defensive errors.
Jamie McCart scored an own goal and Stephen Kingsley contributed to a second Thun goal following poor defending.
Stuart Findlay scored a late consolation header for Hearts, leaving the team with one point from three games.
body: FC Thun vs Hearts; UEFA Conference League
FC Thun vs Hearts. UEFA Conference League.
Stockhorn Arena.
Thun 3-1 Hearts: Wouter Vrancken's side bruised by self-inflicted Conference League defeat

Report as Hearts lose 3-1 to Thun in the Conference League; Jamie McCart's own goal was the first of the errors; Stephen Kingsley gifted another; Stuart Findlay scored a late consolation; the Jambos have one point from their opening three games
Thursday 5 November 2026 23:45, UK
Depleted Hearts' Conference League bruising was almost totally self-inflicted in a 3-1 defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

Belgian boss Wouter Vrancken was without 10 players through various ailments and the Scottish team were dealt another blow in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart put through his own goal in calamitous fashion.

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after more poor defending, this time from skipper Stephen Kingsley - who went off later with an injury - and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute before Jambos defender Stuart Findlay reduced the deficit in the 82nd minute with a header.

Hearts are left with one Conference League point out of nine following a 1-1 home draw against Nordsjaelland and a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

Thick smoke from a pyro halted the game soon after kick-off but when play resumed after a lengthy delay - there were nine minutes added on at the end of the first half - Hearts winger Josh McPake drew a save from Niklas Steffen with an angled drive that lacked real power.
In the 20th minute McPake's effort from 25 yards after he had drifted in from the left had the power but was beaten away by the Thun 'keeper.
There appeared to be nothing untoward on the horizon but then came a Hearts horror show.

There was no real pressure on the Jambos goal when a long ball came into the box but with Lucien Dahler at his shoulder, a simple pass back from McCart somehow evaded Hearts 'keeper Beau Reus and slipped into the corner of the net.
Thun's second goal was also gift-wrapped.

The home side broke clear and with pace following a Heart set-piece and when Nils Reichmuth crossed into the box from the right, Kingsley stuck out a leg to clear but the ball went straight to Labeau who swept it into the net from 10 yards out.
Dursun was shown a yellow card for a forearm challenge into the face of Findlay, and it perhaps deserved more punishment.
The interval gave the Tynecastle side time to reset but, three minutes after the break, Reus made a diving save from Dursun and an even better one from Reichmuth moments later.
However, the 'keeper was beaten once again when Dursun got his toe to a Reichmuth cross.
On the hour mark, Nico Maier raced clear of the Hearts defence but although his chip beat Reus, it sped wide of the target.
The night got worse for the rattled visitors as injured Kingsley was replaced by 19-year-old Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir.
Hearts were sporadic in their threat.
Malachi Fagan-Walcott's header from a Jordi Altena free-kick was brilliantly saved by Steffen.

In the 78th minute Jan Bamert had the ball in the net after Steffen tipped a free-kick from substitute Nassim Zoukit on to the bar but was ruled offside, before Findlay headed in a consolation from another Altena free-kick.
Vrancken demands unity as Hearts seek to bounce back
Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken:
"We have to stick together now. We know which situation we're in with all the circumstances.
"And there's only one thing that you have to do now and that is stick together and keep working hard.
"In general, it was not good enough in quality and can you blame them?
"Yeah, on one hand you can because you want to always expect the best and want the best.
"On the other hand, I'm still proud of what they did already in the run-up games."

articles.headline: Amazon's Black Friday Audible Deal Is Now Live: Pay $0.99 Per Month Plus Get $20 Credit
keyFacts: Amazon launched an Audible Black Friday promotion offering three months of Standard membership for $0.99 per month plus a $20 credit.
The promotion runs from now through December 28 and is available to new and previously expired subscribers.
After the three-month promotional period, subscriptions automatically convert to the standard $8.99 per month rate unless canceled.
body: Black Friday lands on November 27 this year but plenty of deals are already going live now, including Amazon's annual Audible Black Friday promotion. Starting now and running through December 28, both Amazon Prime and non-Prime members can sign up for three months of Audible Standard for $0.99 per month. In addition to the discounted membership, you also get an extra $20 in Audible credit. This deal is valid for new and previous (currently expired) subscribers, however your mileage may vary (we noticed that some this deal doesn't show up for some account). Afterwards your subscription will convert to the standard $8.99/mo, but you can cancel the auto-renewal at any time.
Audible Black Friday Deal: $0.99 Per Month + $20 in Audible Credit
New and previous subscribers

Amazon offers two Audible subscription tiers: Standard and Premium Plus. Standard is a lot less expensive - $8.95 per month compared to $14.95 per month. Standard also gets you access to nearly the same catalog of million plus audiobooks that Premium Plus does. Premium Plus does have an extra "Plus" catalog of about 150,000 books. The main difference, however, lies in the credits: Standard gets one free audiobook per month that you can read so long as you maintain your membership . Premium Plus gets you one free audiobook that you keep indefinitely.

Unless you really want an audiobook to keep every month, then the Standard subscription is the better deal. Most of the popular audiobook series, including Dungeon Crawler Crawl, Hunger Games, The Stormlight Archive, and more, are available in the Standard collection. You'll save $72 on subscription fees per year not including this discount.
Dungeon Crawler Carl audiobooks are on Audible

IGN's Jacob Kienlen is a huge fan of the Dungeon Crawler Carl LitRPG series . He's written about many of the books and just recently the series' first ever graphic novel . The books are all currently available as audiobooks, all narrated by Jeff Hays, who is part of Soundbooth Theater. They also all happen to be free to listen to with an Audible membership.
Catch up on the latest novel releases, audiobook style

Audible is a subscription service that gives you access to over 1.1 million of the best audiobooks without ever having to purchase them. Several best-selling new and recent releases are available in an audiobook format and part of Audible's accessible library. Rebecca Yarros' The Empyrean Series romantasy novels have consistently hit the top of the New York Times' best seller list throughout all of 2025 and they're all available in audiobook format. Sunrise on the Reaping, the latest Hunger Games novel, is narrated by Jefferson White, who you may already know from Yellowstone where he played Jimmy Hudstrom. articles.headline: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
keyFacts: A decade-old vulnerability allows attackers to log into certain Linux devices with no password under specific system configurations.
Alpine maintainers stated that reachable systems can be accessed with a single connection and inputting more than 256 characters.
Security firm Checkpoint reported that root accounts remain safe under default settings, but accounts with sudo rights can still become root.
body: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password.

The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.
One connection, works every time, needs no retries

There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a “*” in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts.
When all the conditions are met, the consequences are high.
“An attacker who can reach your SSH port can log in without knowing any password,” Alpine maintainers said Thursday. “It takes one connection, works every time, and needs no retries.”
When logging into a passwordless account, the attacker can gain access by inputting more than 256 characters in the password field.

Security firm Checkpoint said that the use of the SHA256 or SHA512 functions “matters because sshd borrows that account’s salt. Without it, the attack fails.” Company researchers said their testing also showed that the account must be active, not just hold a hash. Checkpoint further reported that root accounts are safe under the default PermitRootLogin prohibit password setting, though reachable accounts with doas or sudo rights can still become root.

articles.headline: Premier League title winner with Chelsea tipped to succeed Alonso as manager
keyFacts: Former player Lianne Sanderson told talkSPORT that Cesc Fabregas will eventually replace Xabi Alonso as Chelsea manager.
Fabregas is currently managing Italian club Como, which has performed strongly in Serie A and the Champions League under his leadership.
Italian journalist Daniele Fisichella stated that Fabregas is likely to move to a larger club next summer.
body: Cesc Fabregas has been tipped to be the next Chelsea manager after Xabi Alonso.
The former Blues and Arsenal midfielder is winning plenty of fans for the job he is doing as boss of Italian side Como.
Fabregas has been linked to some of the top jobs around Europe Getty
They smashed Lens 9-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday night and look certain to progress to the knockout stage.
Como are also just two points off the top of Serie A and have lost just once all season.
Their rise in the last decade has been staggering, with the club playing in the fourth tier of Italian football as recently as 2019.
In 2022, Fabregas was revealed as a new Como player as the club sat in Serie B .
He invested a minority ownership share when he joined, partnering alongside former Barcelona teammate Thierry Henry with the exact percentage not being publicly disclosed.
Where could Fabregas go next?
Alonso was only hired as Chelsea manager this summer on a four-year contract.
But when has that stopped there being a swift change in the Stamford Bridge dugout?
The Blues are currently fourth in the Premier League, but some fears have been raised early on in his tenure.
This came to the fore in the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham at home with his team selection coming under fire.
Now 50-cap England women’s striker Lianne Sanderson believes Fabregas could be the man to eventually replace him.
Fabregas’ Como have scored 19 goals in four Champions League games Getty
Sanderson told talkSPORT’s Kick-Off: “There’s a lot of conversation about Cesc Fabregas . When you’re a good coach, good manager, he’s going to be linked to different teams.
“My hot take was he’ll be the next Chelsea manager after Xabi Alonso .”
Fabregas at Como
Italian journalist Daniele Fisichella joined the show and admitted he was surprised that Fabregas was still at the Italian club.

He said: “I think we are blessed in Serie A having had him for three seasons already. I thought last summer he would have gone because he received so many criticism in Italy for the way his Como team played.
“Como don’t always win games, but they always play on the front foot. And Cesc made the mistake of telling the Italians, well, you are all about the results and you don’t care how teams play.
“There’s been a lot of criticism because people get a little bit twitchy about it, but then he had the last word last season.
Como are one of the most exciting teams to watch in Europe this season Getty
“I thought that after all this, so much criticism, he would have gone to the Premier League or maybe to La Liga but he actually stayed.

“But I am under no illusion. I think this next summer he moves to a bigger club with no disrespect to Como and so does Nico Paz, so does ‘Tasos’ Douvikas and probably Lucas da Cunha, who’s already played for the French team.
“Cesc is the real deal. He’s got a stronger playing philosophy, but he’s not a fundamentalist. I think he’s taken a leaf out of some of the Italian managers’ books as well.
“This season Como managed games better than last season. Sometimes they’re even happy to defend in a low block.
“He’s not just attack, attack. He’s also a little bit of a pragmatist.”
Fabregas’ budding managerial career follows his stellar playing days which saw him play for elite sides of world football.
The Spaniard controversially moved to Chelsea from Barcelona having spent the first eight years of his career at Arsenal.
But Fabregas enjoyed huge success at Stamford Bridge as he won five trophies, including two Premier League titles.
As well as winning a plethora of trophies at club level, Fabregas was part of the all-star Spain squad that won Euro 2008 and 2012 as well as the 2010 World Cup.

articles.headline: Take on a time-manipulating corporation in the very Soul Eater meets Jet Set Radio action roguelite CHRONO PUNK
keyFacts: CHRONO PUNK is an action roguelite video game featuring fast-paced combat, combo mechanics, and traversal styles like wall-running and swinging.
Players fight a time-manipulating mega corporation that controls the city, either in solo mode or co-op.
The game currently has no release date, but players can wishlist it on Steam.
body: My favourite kind of game that's obviously going for the vibe of a particular era of gaming is one that doesn't look like it's trying to be any other game from said era, moreso if someone told me it was a PS2 or a Dreamcast game everyone forgot about I'd believe you. CHRONO PUNK fits that vibe quite well, an action roguelite that looks like it's taking some cues from those aforementioned consoles, alongside the likes of Soul Eater, Jet Set Radio, Devil May Cry, and Spider-Man.

That is, obviously, a lot of things, but CHRONO PUNK on the surface appears to have its own identity at least. Your player character looks like an almost nightcore version of Sora Kingdom Hearts, with various roles and weapons to choose from; there's a sword and shield, pistols, shurikon, grimoire, and most Soul Eatery of all, a scythe. CHRONO PUNK's got vibes, too. The cities you do combat in are big and nondescript when it comes to details, but ripe for jetting about and Spider-Man-style swinging across the place. And besides, it looks like there's some hub areas ripped straight out of any stylised MMO from the 2000s.

I'm liking the look of the combat too. This'll obviously be one for the combo pilled out there, people who like to bounce back and forth between their enemies like a pinball. Slow paced, this is not. Sick, I hope this is. Pair all of that with some bouncy, wall running movement, and there's some real potential for a strong game here. Sounds like you'll be able to play it in co-op or solo too, which is a nice touch.

The story doesn't seem all that complicated, with some mega corporation manipulating time thereby controlling the city and the masses, leaving you to deal with the mess, but hey, I'm here for the vibes. As of right now, there's no release date attached to CHRONO PUNK, but you can wishlist it on Steam while you wait.

articles.headline: Classic Halo Trilogy Gets Brand-New Release on Nov. 10
keyFacts: Gallery Books will release Halo: The Master Chief Omnibus, a hardcover collection of three classic franchise novels, on Nov. 10.
The collection includes The Fall of Reach and First Strike by Eric Nylund, and The Flood by William C. Dietz.
The novels explore humanity's war against the Covenant, the origins of the Spartan program, and events surrounding the original games.
body: It's been a busy year for Halo fans, with plenty of new releases and surprises keeping the franchise alive. Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the original game, is bringing Master Chief's first adventure to a new generation, while a tabletop adaptation is also in development. Even Halo Infinite isn't quite ready to call it quits, continuing to receive unexpected updates this year despite its major content support coming to an end.

Now, fans looking for even more Halo content have another release to look forward to this holiday season. A new book collection bringing together three classic novels from the franchise is on the way, giving longtime fans and newcomers a chance to revisit some of Master Chief's most important adventures.

Titled Halo: The Master Chief Omnibus, the hardcover collection arrives on Nov. 10, from Gallery Books. It brings together three bestselling novels by authors Eric Nylund and William C. Dietz, alongside a new foreword and additional material.
The new omnibus collects three novels that helped establish the Halo universe's expanded lore: The Fall of Reach and First Strike by Eric Nylund, and The Flood by William C. Dietz.

Originally published as stand-alone books, the novels explore different stages of humanity's war against the Covenant, the alien religious empire threatening humanity's survival. They also provide additional context for Master Chief, the Spartan super-soldier better known as John-117, and the events surrounding the original Halo trilogy.
What are the three Halo novels about?

The collection offers a broad look at the early days of the Halo storyline, starting with the origins of the Spartan program and eventually moving into the conflict that puts humanity's survival at stake.

The Fall of Reach explores the creation and training of the Spartan-II program, including John-117's transformation into the Master Chief. It also chronicles the Covenant's devastating attack on the human military stronghold of Reach, an important event in the franchise's history.

The Flood retells the events of the original Halo: Combat Evolved, expanding on the Master Chief's fight against the Covenant on the mysterious Halo ringworld. The story also introduces the terrifying Flood, a parasitic lifeform that poses an even greater threat to the galaxy.

Finally, First Strike bridges the events of Halo: Combat Evolved and Halo 2. Following the destruction of the first Halo ring, Master Chief and other survivors attempt to return to Earth while uncovering more about the Covenant's plans.

Together, the three novels provide a deeper understanding of the characters, conflicts, and major events that shaped the original Halo games. Halo: The Master Chief Omnibus releases in hardcover on Nov. 10.

articles.headline: What the midterms could mean for Trump’s Cabinet
keyFacts: President Donald Trump's administration faces potential Cabinet shakeups following recent midterm election losses before Democrats take control of Congress.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth are among the officials who could potentially leave the administration.
Trump likely needs to get Cabinet replacements confirmed during the final two months of the current Republican Senate majority.
body: President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at a news conference during the NATO Summit in Ankara, Turkey, on July 8, 2026. | Krisztian Bocsi/Bloomberg via Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: It’s a whole new world for President Donald Trump.

What’s happening? So far, surprisingly little: As we wrote yesterday, Trump has largely stayed quiet since his shellacking in Tuesday’s midterms ( ballroom tour aside), and that continued on Thursday.
With the days counting down until Democrats take control of Congress, though, there are signs that things could begin to shift in his administration.

What could happen? A Cabinet shakeup, whether that means firings, resignations, or something in between. It’s not unusual after any midterm, and especially not after a loss this seismic (Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld stepped down the day after the 2006 midterms amid voter anger about Iraq).

Whatever happens, though, might need to happen fairly soon: It’s always possible that Trump could skate by with acting secretaries (he’s previously said he’s a fan ), but if he wants to get replacements confirmed, he’ll likely need to do it in the final two months of the current Republican Senate majority.
Who’s eyeing the exits? Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth , potentially — but for very different reasons.

In Rubio’s case, it would give him a chance to distance himself from a radioactively unpopular presidency ahead of a potential 2028 presidential run — particularly as Vice President JD Vance is stuck writing social media posts about why the Iran war was maybe a bad idea .

Hegseth, meanwhile, is one of the public faces of the war. Trump has — for now — denied any designs on replacing Hegseth, but the secretary faces the prospect of impeachment as soon as next week. He’s also reportedly interested in being appointed to a soon-to-be-vacant US Senate seat for Tennessee, which would provide him a convenient escape (though based on Tuesday’s results , he might be an underdog to win an election anywhere in America).

What’s the big picture? We don’t yet know anything for sure about what’s next, but the chatter is reflective of the new world Trump and his administration are facing: dismally unpopular, deprived of easy confirmation hearings and cover from Republicans in Congress, and facing an aggressive oversight agenda.
And with that, it’s time to log off…
